known_facts_at_decision_date: J.C. Penney undertook a major strategic repositioning under new leadership beginning early 2012
The company moved away from a coupon and promotional pricing model toward a simplified everyday low pricing strategy
Existing customers were accustomed to promotional pricing, discounts, and coupon-based shopping behavior
The strategy attempted to change customer behavior and brand perception simultaneously across the full chain
The change carried traffic risk, conversion risk, customer-segmentation risk, price-perception risk, and brand-fit risk
The repositioning was implemented without public evidence of prior customer-behavior validation or pilot testing
The risk of abrupt change was identifiable: if core customers did not respond to everyday pricing, traffic and conversion would decline before new customers arrived

financial_signals_at_decision_date.pricing_model_change: From promotional/coupon to everyday low price — full chain rollout
financial_signals_at_decision_date.revenue_risk: High — traffic and conversion dependent on customer behavior change
financial_signals_at_decision_date.investment_required: Yes — brand repositioning and marketing to support new model
financial_signals_at_decision_date.pilot_testing: Not publicly disclosed as of decision date
financial_signals_at_decision_date.customer_base_dependency: High reliance on existing promo-sensitive customers

operating_signals_at_decision_date.store_format: Full-chain implementation of new pricing model
operating_signals_at_decision_date.customer_segmentation: Existing customers highly promo-sensitive by historical behavior
operating_signals_at_decision_date.brand_change_scope: Broad — name shortened to JCP, store redesign, pricing model change
operating_signals_at_decision_date.change_management: Abrupt full-chain rollout without disclosed phased approach
operating_signals_at_decision_date.new_leadership: CEO Ron Johnson from Apple — imported Apple retail strategy concepts

governance_signals_at_decision_date.leadership_mandate: New CEO implementing aggressive strategic repositioning
governance_signals_at_decision_date.board_support: Supportive of strategy at decision date
governance_signals_at_decision_date.customer_feedback_loop: No disclosed real-time traffic/conversion monitoring framework

risk_flags_at_decision_date: Core customers are promo-sensitive — removing promotions without validation risks immediate traffic loss
Full-chain rollout removes ability to use control stores to measure impact
Brand repositioning + pricing change + name change simultaneously increases execution risk
Executive transplant from Apple: toy retail strategy may not transfer to department store
No disclosed pilot: if customer behavior does not shift, damage is chain-wide immediately
Recovery from failed pricing strategy is slow and costly
question: Given the abrupt full-chain shift from promotional pricing to everyday low pricing, without disclosed pilot testing, targeting a customer base with strong promo-sensitivity, diagnose the main risks and recommend the highest-priority action plan to protect the core customer base while pursuing the repositioning.
